sites.name: Bat Pagoda (Mahatup Pagoda)
sites.event: A famous Khmer pagoda known for its unique architecture and as a sanctuary for thousands of giant flying foxes.

sites.name: Nga Nam Floating Market
sites.event: The intersection of 5 rivers flowing in 5 directions (Ca Mau, Vinh Quoi, Long My, Thanh Tri, Phung Hiep), a characteristic feature of river culture.

sites.name: Chen Kieu Pagoda (Sa Lon Pagoda)
sites.event: A Khmer pagoda with brilliant architecture, decorated with millions of broken pieces of bowls, plates, and porcelain, creating unique patterns.

sites.name: Clay Pagoda (Buu Son Tu)
sites.event: Famous for thousands of Buddha statues and mythical beasts made of clay, and giant pairs of candles that burn for decades without going out.

sites.name: Tan Long Stork Garden
sites.event: A private sanctuary, home to thousands of storks and night herons, creating a pristine natural landscape in the middle of the delta.

sites.name: Kh'leang Pagoda
sites.event: The oldest pagoda in Soc Trang (built around 1533), associated with the legend of the origin of the name Soc Trang.

sites.name: My Phuoc Islet
sites.event: Known as the 'fruit kingdom' in the middle of the Hau River, famous for its lush orchards (longan, rambutan, durian).

sites.name: Soc Trang Provincial Party Committee Base (My Phuoc Melaleuca Forest)
sites.event: An important revolutionary base during the two resistance wars, located in the middle of a vast melaleuca forest.

sites.name: Som Rong Pagoda (Wat Patum Wongsa Som Rong)
sites.event: Famous for its giant outdoor reclining Buddha statue and a magnificent palace-like stupa.

sites.name: Soc Trang Khmer Museum
sites.event: A place that preserves and displays many valuable artifacts reflecting the cultural, spiritual, and historical life of the Khmer ethnic people.

sites.name: Ho Be Beach
sites.event: A pristine beach with long, smooth sand and a coastal mangrove forest ecosystem.
